SendEmailAccount.description:
One SMTP account on the relay, as OPI created it (one per cluster).

Shaped like ``KeycloakRealm``: matched on ``cluster``, written by the platform, and
the only place this account's password lives. ``extra="allow"`` so a field added later
does not make existing project files unreadable.

bounce-address.description: Address bounces for this account return to; carries the project name so a bounce is traceable.
bounce-address.title: Bounce-Address

cluster.description: Cluster this account was created for. Written by the platform.
cluster.title: Cluster

from-address.description: Address the relay pins the envelope sender and the From: header to for this account.
from-address.title: From-Address

username.description: SASL username the application authenticates to the relay with.
username.title: Username

SendEmailAccount.title: SendEmailAccount

SendEmailApproval.description:
Whether an administrator has allowed this project to send mail (aanvulling 6).

Shaped like the domain/subdomain entries publish-on-web stores: a status plus the
verdict history, so the file is the audit trail. Written only through the generic
approval flow (``opi/services/approvals.py``).

history.description: Verdict history: one {date, status, by, message} entry per decision.
history.title: History

status.description: requested, approved or denied. Written by the platform's approval flow.
status.title: Status

SendEmailApproval.title: SendEmailApproval

SendEmailValueApproval.description:
Whether an administrator approved a requested VALUE (address or budget).

Hangs on the VALUE, not the project: if approved for one value and the project changes
it, that is a new request. Both address and budget use this shape; both are text so a
single shape fits both.

approved-value.description: The last value an administrator approved, which keeps applying while a new request is open.
approved-value.title: Approved-Value

history.description: Verdict history: one {date, status, by, message} entry per decision.
history.title: History

status.description: requested, approved or denied. Written by the platform's approval flow.
status.title: Status

value.description: The value this verdict is about. Written by the platform's approval flow.
value.title: Value

SendEmailValueApproval.title: SendEmailValueApproval

description: What a project may decide about its outgoing mail.

accounts.description: Per-cluster SMTP accounts on the relay. Written and managed by the platform: carried over on a write, so a caller neither has to send it nor can lose it by leaving it out.
accounts.title: Accounts

approval.description: Whether an administrator has allowed this project to send mail. Written by the platform: until it says approved, no account is created, no network policy is written and no SMTP credentials reach the deployment.

from-address.description: Sender address this project asks to send from, e.g. 'noreply@rijksoverheid.nl'. It only takes effect once a platform administrator has approved that exact value; until then the platform composes the address from the project name. Leave it out for the composed address. Het afzenderadres moet een adres in rijksoverheid.nl zijn, met voor de @ hoogstens 64 tekens uit kleine letters, cijfers en . _ + - (bijvoorbeeld noreply@rijksoverheid.nl). Een ander domein lijnt niet uit met de envelope en komt niet door DMARC.
from-address.title: From-Address

from-address-approval.description: Whether an administrator has allowed the requested sender address. Written by the platform: until it says approved for exactly the address in from-address, the relay keeps deriving the address from the project name.

from-name.description: Display name shown to the recipient, e.g. 'Algoritmeregister'. The relay puts this in the From: header next to the project's address, so it may not contain control characters, an @, angle brackets, quotes, a backslash or a dollar sign, and it is at most 64 characters. Leave it out to send without a display name.
from-name.title: From-Name

messages-per-day.description: Messages per day, enforced by the relay per account. Up to and including the platform default, the project chooses; above that is a REQUEST requiring approval. The 1000000 ceiling only catches typos.
messages-per-day.title: Messages-Per-Day

messages-per-day-approval.description: Whether an administrator approved the requested budget. Until approved for exactly the requested number, the relay enforces the last approved number or the default.
